source: Muse recheck of first-pass flags; apply through the belt (02 fact block -> 16 -> 04/05 remint), never in place

corrections.corrected_statement: To add the For-Hire endorsement you must pay four dollars and fifty cents, be at least eighteen years old, be operating a Class D vehicle, and have two years of unrestricted driving experience.
corrections.note: Corrected to separate unrestricted experience from the Class D operation requirement.

corrections.corrected_statement: A temporary driver license or temporary identification license is issued for the period of authorized stay up to a maximum of five years for a base cost of twenty eight dollars that does not change with length but extra fees still apply for graduated licensing and motorcycle and for hire endorsements and for each additional license type.
corrections.note: Added that extra graduated, motorcycle, for hire and multiple type fees apply on top of base cost.

corrections.corrected_statement: Belted occupants who do strike the wheel, dashboard or windshield usually hit with far less force and suffer less serious injury.
corrections.note: The force and injury clause is printed on page 46, not page 45.

corrections.corrected_statement: A childs lap belt should lie securely on the upper thigh low and snug around the hips.
corrections.note: Removed adult pelvis and thighs wording that page 47 does not state.

corrections.corrected_statement: Keep your speed until you are in the deceleration lane, then slow to the ramp's posted speed and on to the limit of the road you are joining.
corrections.note: Maintain-speed clause is on page 83, not fully on cited page 84.

corrections.corrected_statement: At a weaving interchange be aware that vehicles already on the interstate may be moving right toward the exit ramp and both you and the other driver must yield and share in an equal give and take manner.
corrections.note: Page does not say entering driver moves left.

corrections.corrected_statement: HELP operators may remove any vehicle that obstructs or endangers traffic, and you must follow their directions as you would a police officer's.

A roadside kit should include a good spare tire, jack and tire iron, pressure gauge, flashlight with spare batteries, first aid kit, fire extinguisher, jumper cables, three fuses or reflectors, insurance and registration papers, and a cell phone.
corrections.note: Page lists fuses or reflectors, not reflectors or flares.

corrections.corrected_statement: Communicate in traffic with your horn, lights and signals and be reasonably sure of people's intentions.
corrections.note: Removed the added timing phrase not stated on the page.

corrections.corrected_statement: Communicating in traffic means making your next move clear to drivers and pedestrians in time for them to avoid a collision.
corrections.note: The definition begins on the prior page, not the cited page.

corrections.corrected_statement: Never turn the ignition to the lock position while the car is moving, because the steering wheel will lock and you will lose control.
corrections.note: The lock-consequence completion is printed on page 115, not page 114.

corrections.corrected_statement: On narrow bridges and in tunnels, approaching vehicles pass closer together, so adjust your speed.
corrections.note: The narrow-bridges sentence starts on page 115, not page 116.
